title: Audit Change Patch Index and Actor Context Annotations for RBAC v2 Admin Actions
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and roll out a new audit event shape that focuses on an append-only change_patch_index plus rich actor annotations for RBAC v2 admin/privileged actions. Goal: make admin changes queryable by changed path, reconstructible for troubleshooting, and provably associated with an identity chain (SSO/SAML assertion, session, proxies) while supporting redaction and retention tiers.
proposed_schema: Event fields (flat string list description): event_id, occurred_at, service, action, severity, outcome, correlation_id, trace_id, actor_id, actor_type, actor_identity_provider, actor_session_id, actor_mfa, actor_confidence, actor_assertion_id, actor_proxy_chain, client_ip, user_agent, target_id, target_type, target_namespace, change_patch_index_reference, change_patch_index_inline, pre_state_snapshot_ref, post_state_snapshot_ref, sensitivity_tags, retention_tier, storage_location, signature, idempotency_key
patch_encoding: Change patch encoding: op-based compact patch list (one-line per op) using a small op grammar: OP|PATH|FROM|TO where OP in {ADD,REMOVE,REPLACE,MERGE}. Examples: 'REPLACE|/roles/role-123/members|[user:alice]|[user:alice,user:bob]'; 'REMOVE|/policies/policy-77|{...}|null'. Patches may be stored inline for small changes (change_patch_index_inline) or as a signed blob reference (change_patch_index_reference) for larger diffs. Blobs are SHA256 keyed and encrypted. Patches must be canonicalized (sorted keys, deterministic serialization) to enable easy hashing and deduplication.
actor_context: Actor annotations include confidence and provenance fields: actor_identity_provider (e.g., okta-saml), actor_assertion_id (SAML Response or Assertion ID), actor_session_id, actor_proxy_chain (comma-separated host:port or service ids), actor_mfa (true/false), actor_confidence (0.0-1.0 string), client_ip, geo_hint, user_agent. When a change is performed by an automation/service account, include upstream_user_hint and service_token_id. These fields must be present on all admin action events to support auditability and automated risk scoring.
target_context: Target annotations describe resource identity and snapshot pointers: target_id (stable GUID), target_type (role, policy, org, cluster), target_namespace, pre_state_snapshot_ref (optional shard:key), post_state_snapshot_ref (optional shard:key), sensitivity_tags (comma-separated), change_reason_code, human_reason. Snapshots are stored as versioned JSON blobs; snapshot refs are opaque references with retention metadata.
correlation_and_routing: All events include correlation_id and trace_id. Routing/sharding keys: primary_by = actor_id, secondary_by = target_id, sequence_bucket = date-hour. Consumers should be able to stream events by actor_id or by change_path (index on path tokens) for efficient lookups. Events include an event_sequence_number for the service stream to preserve causal ordering.
retention_and_access_controls: Retention tiers: short-term (90d), medium (1y), long-term (7y) for high-sensitivity records. Sensitive fields (e.g., pre_state snapshot with PII) stored encrypted and accessible only via audit-read roles; events expose redaction pointers if redaction applied. Retention and redaction flags are annotated on each event. KMS key id and envelope metadata must be recorded for every encrypted blob.
storage_and_immutability: Append-only, immutable ledger semantics: write-once events with monotonic event_sequence_number per service. New corrective actions must be represented as new events, not in-place mutation. Each event includes a signature (service-signature) and optional external-signature for high assurance flows. Idempotency: producers must include idempotency_key; duplicates with same idempotency_key are deduplicated at write time and emit a duplicate_notice event.
query_patterns: Primary queries we must optimize for: (1) all changes by actor_id within time range; (2) all changes touching a path token (e.g., '/roles/*/members'); (3) reconstruct state for a target_id at a given timestamp by applying patches in sequence; (4) SSO-linked investigations by actor_assertion_id. Indexes: actor_id, actor_assertion_id, target_id, path_token, event_time, retention_tier.
backward_compatibility_migration: Migration plan: run a producer shim that emits both legacy_event_shape and new_event_shape for 4 weeks; ETL job to compute change_patch_index_reference where legacy logs included full JSON mutations. Provide a consumer library that maps legacy fields to new names (actor -> actor_id, assertion -> actor_assertion_id, diff -> change_patch_index_inline) until all services graduate.
acceptance_criteria: Schema doc reviewed and signed off by Security and Product
Producer SDK updated to emit the new event shape and idempotency_key
Storage layer accepts reference blobs (signed, encrypted) and enforces retention annotations
End-to-end test: reconstruct role membership from patches and match expected state for 3 sample scenarios
Audit read workflows updated (console and API) to show actor provenance (SSO link) and allow downloading signed change patches
tasks: Finalize event field list and publish JSON schema spec
Implement producer SDK changes and feature flag the new shape
Add patch blob store with encryption and signed references
Add indexes for path_token and actor_assertion_id
Update console audit UI to show actor chain and patch diffs
Run migration shim and monitor duplicate rate
Security review and threat model update
notes: We intentionally choose op-based patches rather than full pre/post snapshots for most admin events to reduce storage and make intent explicit.
Signed blob references enable lightweight events in the main stream while preserving forensic detail in the blob store.
Ensure SAML assertion IDs are scrubbed for privacy concerns in low-retention tiers; use redaction pointers instead.
Actor confidence is used by the risk engine to auto-open high-risk review tickets for out-of-band changes.
